description: The individual shape libraries listed in the More Shapes dialog (Software, Networking, Business and Other sections) with their sidebar keys, sub-palettes and the shape-name prefixes they generate, plus the dialog and search features used to enable and find shapes. Keys are the values accepted by the libs= URL parameter and the defaultLibraries / enabledLibraries configuration keys.

tools.name: More Shapes... dialog and library keys
tools.description: Opened from the bottom of the shape sidebar (+ More Shapes...) or the ?libs= parameter, this dialog lists every built-in library grouped as Standard (general, basic, arrows2, clipart, flowchart), Software (active_directory, android, atlassian2, atlassian, bootstrap, c4, dfd, er, ios, mockups, sitemap, salesforce, uml25, uml), Networking (alibaba_cloud, allied_telesis, aws3, aws4b, aws4, aws4r, aws3d, azure2, mscae, cisco, cisco19, cisco_safe, cumulus, citrix2, citrix, dynamics365, gcp2, gcp3, gcpicons, ibm, ibm_cloud, kubernetes, network2, network, office, openstack, rack, sap, veeam2, vvd), Business (archimate4, archimate3, archimate, bpmn2, sysml, lean_mapping) and Other (cabinets, infographic, eip, electrical, floorplan, fluid_power, gmdl, pid, threatModeling, webicons, signs). Ticking a library adds it to the sidebar; the choice is stored in browser settings.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Library key as listed above, e.g. aws4, azure2, cisco19.

parameters.name: Apply
parameters.description: Rebuilds the sidebar with the selected libraries.

tools.example: https://app.diagrams.net/?splash=0&libs=general;flowchart;aws4;kubernetes;c4
tools.notes: enabledLibraries restricts what the dialog offers; defaultLibraries sets what is shown initially. Removing a library from the sidebar does not affect existing diagrams that use its shapes.

tools.name: Search Shapes (sidebar search)
tools.description: The search box at the top of the shape sidebar (library key search) matches shape titles and tags across all enabled and disabled built-in libraries and, when online, also returns icons from the Iconfinder service. Results appear as a temporary palette; drag or click to insert. The ?search-shapes= parameter pre-fills the query.
tools.usage: Sidebar > Search Shapes > type a term > Enter (or click a result)

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Free text, e.g. database, firewall, lambda.

parameters.name: More results
parameters.description: Loads the next page of matches.

tools.example: Type "kubernetes pod" and press Enter; drag the Pod shape from the results onto the canvas.
tools.notes: Search only covers libraries whose shapes are indexed; custom libraries are not searched. Extended icon results are disabled in offline/stealth mode.

tools.name: mxgraph.* shape name prefixes (reference)
tools.description: Most library shapes are stencils whose style starts with shape=mxgraph.<library>.<name>. Common prefixes: mxgraph.flowchart, mxgraph.basic, mxgraph.arrows2, mxgraph.bpmn, mxgraph.er, mxgraph.uml25 (UML 2.5), mxgraph.aws4, mxgraph.aws3d, mxgraph.mscae (Cloud & Enterprise), mxgraph.azure, mxgraph.gcp2, mxgraph.ibm, mxgraph.kubernetes, mxgraph.cisco19, mxgraph.cisco, mxgraph.cisco_safe, mxgraph.network, mxgraph.rack.<vendor>, mxgraph.office.<category>, mxgraph.veeam2, mxgraph.vvd, mxgraph.c4, mxgraph.archimate3, mxgraph.sysml, mxgraph.lean_mapping, mxgraph.eip, mxgraph.electrical.<category>, mxgraph.pid2<group>, mxgraph.mockup.<category>, mxgraph.bootstrap, mxgraph.android, mxgraph.ios7, mxgraph.gmdl, mxgraph.infographic, mxgraph.signs.<category>, mxgraph.webicons, mxgraph.cabinets, mxgraph.floorplan, mxgraph.dfd and mxgraph.sitemap. Image-based libraries (azure2, gcp3, gcpicons, clipart, atlassian2, dynamics365) use shape=image;image=img/lib/... instead.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Shape name; find it via Edit > Edit Style on a placed shape.

tools.example: shape=mxgraph.aws4.lambda_function;   shape=mxgraph.cisco19.rect;prIcon=router;   shape=mxgraph.office.users.user;   shape=mxgraph.electrical.logic_gates.logic_gate;operation=and;
tools.notes: Stencil definitions live under src/main/webapp/stencils/*.xml in the jgraph/drawio repository; some libraries (cisco19, aws4 groups, c4) are JavaScript shapes with extra style keys such as prIcon, grIcon, resIcon or c4Type.

tools.name: Active Directory (active_directory) shape library
tools.description: Microsoft Active Directory topology symbols: forests, domains, sites, domain controllers, organisational units, users, groups, trusts, GPOs and replication links. Use it for identity and directory architecture diagrams alongside the Office and Network libraries.
tools.example: Enable the library, drag Domain Controller and Site shapes, connect them with the default connector styled dashed=1 for replication.
tools.notes: Shapes are drawn in the classic Microsoft grey/blue style; icon colours can be changed through fillColor on most entries.

tools.name: Atlassian (atlassian2) shape library
tools.description: Current Atlassian product and work-type iconography in three palettes: Apps (Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket, Trello, Opsgenie, ...), Work Types (epic, story, task, bug, sub-task, incident) and Logos. The older single-palette Atlassian (legacy) library remains available under key atlassian. Useful for workflow and tooling diagrams that reference Atlassian products.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: atlassian2 (Apps, Work Types, Logos) or atlassian (legacy).

tools.example: Insert the Jira issue-type icons from Work Types next to swimlanes to document a ticket workflow.
tools.notes: Icons are SVG images (shape=image), so they scale losslessly but cannot be recoloured with fillColor.

tools.name: Data Flow Diagram (dfd) shape library
tools.description: Yourdon/DeMarco and Gane-Sarson data-flow symbols: external entity, process (circle and rounded rectangle variants), data store (open-ended rectangle), data flow connectors and level annotations. Use it for structured-analysis DFDs and threat-model context diagrams.
tools.usage: More Shapes > Software > Data Flow Diagram   |   ?libs=dfd
tools.example: shape=mxgraph.dfd.dataStoreID;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;   (data store with id compartment)
tools.notes: Threat Modeling (threatModeling) adds trust boundaries that pair with these shapes.

tools.name: Salesforce (salesforce) shape library
tools.description: Salesforce architecture diagram kit in four palettes: Components, Product, Platform and Industry, following the official Salesforce diagram style (cards, clouds and product icons). Use it for CRM integration and solution-architecture diagrams.
tools.example: Combine Platform cards with the AWS 20xx and Azure libraries to show a hybrid integration landscape.
tools.notes: Product icons are provided as image shapes with fixed aspect ratio.

tools.name: UML 2.5 (uml25) shape library
tools.description: Modern UML 2.5 library that replaces the legacy UML palette with correctly styled class, component, deployment, use case, activity, state machine, sequence, communication, timing and interaction-overview elements, including stereotyped classifiers, ports, lifelines with execution specifications, fragments and pins. Elements are containers with stack layouts where the notation requires compartments.
tools.example: Drag a Class from UML 2.5: the attributes and operations compartments are stackLayout children; press Enter on the last row to add another member.
tools.notes: The legacy uml library (key uml) is kept for old diagrams; new work should use uml25. Sequence-diagram lifelines use shape=umlLifeline with participant styles.

tools.name: Alibaba Cloud (alibaba_cloud) shape library
tools.description: Official Alibaba Cloud product icons (ECS, OSS, RDS, SLB, VPC, CDN, Function Compute, MaxCompute, and so on) for architecture diagrams of deployments on Alibaba Cloud. Single palette, image-based icons with fixed aspect ratio.
tools.example: Place VPC as a container (container=1) and drop ECS and RDS icons inside; label them with verticalLabelPosition=bottom.
tools.notes: Icons cannot be recoloured; use group boxes from General for zones.

tools.name: Allied Telesis (allied_telesis) shape library
tools.description: Vendor library for Allied Telesis networking hardware: Buildings, Computer and Terminals, Media Converters, Security, Storage, Switch and Wireless palettes with realistic device drawings. Use it for physical network diagrams that must show specific product families.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: allied_telesis (palettes: Buildings, Computer and Terminals, Media Converters, Security, Storage, Switch, Wireless)

tools.example: Combine Switch and Wireless devices with the Network 2025 library's generic clients and links.
tools.notes: Device images are detailed; keep aspect=fixed to avoid distortion.

tools.name: AWS 3D (aws3d) shape library
tools.description: Isometric (3D) AWS icons and platform tiles for presentation-style architecture diagrams: instances, storage, databases, networking and containers drawn in the AWS isometric perspective, with isometric edge routing (edgeStyle=isometricEdgeStyle) for connections. Not an official AWS icon set; use aws4 for standard diagrams.
tools.example: shape=mxgraph.aws3d.ec2;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;   connected with   edgeStyle=isometricEdgeStyle;elbow=vertical;
tools.notes: The Format panel Waypoints dropdown offers Isometric routing to match the perspective; View > Grid can be switched to an isometric grid in the Diagram tab.

tools.name: Cloud & Enterprise (mscae) shape library
tools.description: Microsoft Cloud and Enterprise symbol set (the pre-azure2 official Microsoft architecture icons): flat service icons grouped as AI and ML, Analytics, Compute, Container, Databases, DevOps, General, Identity, Integration, IoT, Intune, Management and Governance, Migrate, Mixed Reality, Mobile, Networking, Security, Storage and Web services, plus Companies, EnterpriseFlat, IntuneFlat, OMSFlat and System CenterFlat palettes. Shapes use the prefix mxgraph.mscae and can be recoloured.
tools.example: shape=mxgraph.mscae.enterprise.server;fillColor=#0078d4;
tools.notes: For current Azure icons use azure2; mscae remains for legacy diagrams and on-premises System Center / Intune symbols.

tools.name: Cisco19 (cisco19) shape library
tools.description: Cisco's 2019 icon set: LAN Switching, Routing WAN, Network Management, Data Center, Wireless LAN, Collaboration, Security Clouds Connectors, Endpoint Client Device Icons, DNA SD Access, SD WAN Viptela, ETA Stealthwatch and SAFE palettes. Icons are drawn as one JavaScript shape (mxgraph.cisco19.rect) parameterised by prIcon, so the icon and its background tile can be recoloured with fillColor/strokeColor.

parameters.name: prIcon
parameters.description: Icon id inside the tile, e.g. router, l2_switch, firewall, wireless_router, server.

tools.example: shape=mxgraph.cisco19.rect;prIcon=l3_switch;fillColor=#FAFAFA;strokeColor=#005073;html=1;verticalLabelPosition=bottom;verticalAlign=top;
tools.notes: The older cisco library (key cisco: Buildings, Computers and Peripherals, Controllers and Modules, Directors, Hubs and Gateways, ...) contains the classic 3D Cisco stencils.

tools.name: Cisco Safe (cisco_safe) shape library
tools.description: Symbols of the Cisco SAFE security reference architecture: Architecture, Business Icons, Capability, Design, IoT Things Icons, People Places Things Icons, Security Icons, Technology Icons and Threat palettes. Use it to draw SAFE business flows, capability maps and threat diagrams in Cisco's official notation.
tools.example: Lay out a business flow with People/Places/Things icons on the left and Capability icons in the lanes to the right.
tools.notes: Shapes are stencils with prefix mxgraph.cisco_safe and accept fillColor for the capability tiles.

tools.name: Cumulus (cumulus) shape library
tools.description: NVIDIA/Cumulus Networks data-centre network symbols: spine and leaf switches, servers, virtual machines, containers, cloud and internet nodes, drawn in the Cumulus documentation style for leaf-spine and EVPN fabric diagrams.
tools.example: Build a two-spine/four-leaf fabric: drop Spine and Leaf switches, then Arrange > Layout > Horizontal Flow to align the tiers.
tools.notes: Pairs well with the Rack library for physical placement views.

tools.name: Citrix (citrix2) shape library
tools.description: Current Citrix product iconography in eight palettes: Authentication, Cloud Services, Components, Locations, NetScaler, Networking, Resources and Users and Devices. The previous single-palette set stays available as Citrix (legacy), key citrix. Use it for Citrix Virtual Apps and Desktops, ADC/NetScaler and Workspace architecture diagrams.
tools.example: Place NetScaler ADC between the Users and Devices icons and the Resources (Delivery Controller, StoreFront) icons.
tools.notes: citrix2 icons are SVG images; the legacy citrix set consists of stencils with prefix mxgraph.citrix.

tools.name: Dynamics365 (dynamics365) shape library
tools.description: Microsoft Dynamics 365 icon set with App, Mixed Reality, Product Family and Sub App palettes (Sales, Customer Service, Field Service, Finance, Supply Chain, Business Central, Remote Assist, Guides, ...). Use it with azure2 and Office shapes for Microsoft business-application landscapes.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: dynamics365 (palettes: App, Mixed Reality, Product Family, Sub App)

tools.example: Show a Power Platform integration by combining Dynamics365 App icons with azure2 Power Platform icons.
tools.notes: Image-based icons with fixed aspect ratio.

tools.name: Google Cloud Platform 2026 (gcp3) and GCP Icons (gcpicons) shape libraries
tools.description: gcp3 is the newest Google Cloud architecture kit (Categories and Core Products palettes with the official product cards) and gcpicons is the flat product-icon set organised by area: AI and Machine Learning, API Management, Compute, Data Analytics, Databases, Developer Tools, Expanded Product Card Icons, Generic, Hybrid and Multi Cloud, Security, Internet of Things, Management Tools, Migration, Networking, Open Source Icons and Storage. The older gcp2 library (Paths, Zones, Service Cards, ... product cards) remains for existing diagrams.
tools.usage: More Shapes > Networking > Google Cloud Platform 2026 / GCP Icons   |   ?libs=gcp3;gcpicons

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: gcp3, gcpicons (and gcp2 for the previous kit)

tools.example: Use gcp2 Zones for the outer boxes (Project, VPC, Zone) and gcpicons for the services inside them.
tools.notes: gcp3 and gcpicons icons are images; gcp2 zone/card shapes are stencils (mxgraph.gcp2.*) and can be recoloured.

tools.name: IBM (ibm) shape library
tools.description: IBM Cloud architecture notation (the 'IBM Design' style): Analytics, Applications, Blockchain, Data, DevOps, Infrastructure, Management, Miscellaneous, Security, Social, Users and VPC icon palettes plus Boxes (zone containers with icon badges) and Connectors. Shapes use prefix mxgraph.ibm and support the IBM colour conventions for zones (public network, cloud, enterprise network).
tools.example: shape=mxgraph.ibm.box;prType=cloud;fontStyle=1;verticalAlign=top;align=left;spacingLeft=32;spacingTop=4;container=1;
tools.notes: The separate IBM Cloud library (ibm_cloud) contains the newer IBM Cloud reference-architecture icons.

tools.name: IBM Cloud (ibm_cloud) shape library
tools.description: Newer IBM Cloud reference-architecture symbols: Groups (zones such as Public Network, IBM Cloud, VPC, Subnet, Enterprise), Actors, AI, Compute, Containers, Data, DevOps, Network, Observability, Security and Storage palettes with Connectors. Use it for IBM Cloud solution diagrams following the IBM Cloud architecture guidelines.
tools.example: Nest Groups: Public Network > IBM Cloud > VPC > Subnet, then place Compute and Data icons in the subnet group.
tools.notes: Group shapes are containers; icons keep a fixed aspect ratio.

tools.name: Network 2025 (network2) shape library
tools.description: Refreshed vendor-neutral network symbol set (2025 edition) for logical and physical network diagrams: routers, switches, firewalls, load balancers, wireless access points, servers, storage, clients, phones, clouds, WAN links and buildings, in a consistent modern flat style. The previous Network 2018 set stays available as key network.
tools.usage: More Shapes > Networking > Network 2025   |   ?libs=network2   (2018 set: network)
tools.example: Enable network2, drag Firewall and Core Switch, and use the Arrows library's block arrows for WAN links.
tools.notes: Shapes are recolourable stencils; the 2018 set uses prefix mxgraph.network.

tools.name: Office (office) shape library
tools.description: Microsoft Office/Exchange/SharePoint/Lync visio-style symbol set with ten palettes: Clouds, Communications, Concepts, Databases, Devices, Security, Servers, Services, Sites and Users. Shapes are stencils named mxgraph.office.<palette>.<name> (e.g. mxgraph.office.servers.exchange_server, mxgraph.office.users.user, mxgraph.office.databases.database) and are widely used for on-premises Microsoft infrastructure diagrams.
tools.example: shape=mxgraph.office.servers.file_server;html=1;verticalLabelPosition=bottom;verticalAlign=top;
tools.notes: The library reproduces the colours of the original Microsoft Visio stencils; fillColor changes are limited to some shapes.

tools.name: OpenStack (openstack) shape library
tools.description: OpenStack project icons (Nova, Neutron, Cinder, Swift, Keystone, Glance, Heat, Horizon, Ironic, Magnum, ...) in four colour palettes: Blue, Grey, Green and Red. Use it for private-cloud architecture diagrams; pick one palette per diagram for consistency.
tools.example: Draw a control plane with Keystone, Nova, Neutron and Glance icons (Blue palette) and compute nodes with the Cumulus or Rack libraries.
tools.notes: Icons are images with fixed aspect ratio.

tools.name: SAP (sap) shape library
tools.description: SAP solution-diagram notation covering Annotations, Area Shapes, BTP SaaS, Colored Connectors, Foundations, Integration Suite, App Dev Automation, Data Analytics, AI, Generic Icons, Component Groups, Components, Default Connectors, Default Shapes, Numbers, Other, Products, Build Workzone, Semantic Accent and Texts palettes, following SAP's Business Technology Platform diagramming guidelines.
tools.example: Use Area Shapes for SAP BTP / S/4HANA zones, Components for services and Colored Connectors for the integration flows.
tools.notes: Connector palettes are preset edge styles; drop them and re-attach the ends.

tools.name: Veeam (veeam2) shape library
tools.description: Veeam Backup & Replication and Veeam ONE symbols (2019+ style): Auxiliary, Data Center, Features, General, Products and Components, Software, States, Storage and 3D palettes with backup servers, proxies, repositories, WAN accelerators, tape, VMs and status badges. The older set (key veeam) has Data Center, Misc, Software, Storage, UsersStatus, VASComponents, Backup Replication, Products, VMs and Tape, 2D and 3D palettes.
tools.example: shape=mxgraph.veeam2.backup_repository;html=1;verticalLabelPosition=bottom;verticalAlign=top;
tools.notes: Shapes are stencils (mxgraph.veeam2.*, mxgraph.veeam.*).

tools.name: VMware (vvd) shape library
tools.description: VMware Validated Design (VVD) icon set: vSphere, vCenter, ESXi hosts, NSX, vSAN, vRealize/Aria, Horizon, clusters, virtual machines, networks and storage, drawn in the VMware documentation style. Use it for SDDC and virtualisation architecture diagrams.
tools.example: shape=mxgraph.vvd.esxi;html=1;   inside a cluster container from General.
tools.notes: Stencils with prefix mxgraph.vvd; most accept fillColor.

tools.name: Rack (rack) vendor sub-libraries
tools.description: Rack-elevation shapes in unit-accurate sizes: General (empty racks, blank 1U-4U units, patch panels, shelves, PDUs, cable managers) plus vendor palettes APC, Cisco, Dell, F5, HP, HPE Aruba Gateways Controllers, HPE Aruba Security, HPE Aruba Switches, IBM and Oracle. The rack cabinet is a container with a stack layout so devices snap into rack units; the horizontalRack key is used for horizontally drawn racks.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: rack (palettes: General, APC, Cisco, Dell, F5, HP, HPE Aruba ..., IBM, Oracle)

parameters.name: shape prefix
parameters.description: mxgraph.rack.general.*, mxgraph.rack.cisco.*, mxgraph.rack.dell.*, mxgraph.rack.hp.*, mxgraph.rack.apc.*, mxgraph.rack.f5.*, mxgraph.rack.ibm.*, mxgraph.rack.oracle.*

tools.example: shape=mxgraph.rack.general.1u_rack_server;html=1;labelPosition=right;align=left;spacingLeft=15;   dropped into   shape=mxgraph.rackGeneral.rackCabinet3;fillColor2=#f4f4f4;container=1;collapsible=0;childLayout=rack;
tools.notes: 1U equals 14.8 px at the library's default scale; the cabinet's rack numbering (numDisp, unitSize) is configurable in the Property panel. The f5 plugin adds extra F5 hardware.

tools.name: ArchiMate 4 (archimate4) shape library
tools.description: Enterprise-architecture notation for the ArchiMate 4 specification: Common, Relationships and Junctions, Motivation, Strategy, Business, Application, Technology and Implementation and Migration palettes with the standard layer colours and element icons. The ArchiMate 3.2 library (key archimate3) and the ArchiMate 2.1 library (key archimate) remain for older models.
tools.usage: More Shapes > Business > ArchiMate 4   |   ?libs=archimate4   (3.2: archimate3, 2.1: archimate)
tools.example: Drop a Business Process (yellow), an Application Component (blue) and a Node (green) and connect them with the Relationships palette's Serving and Realization connectors.
tools.notes: ArchiMate 3 shapes are styled shape=mxgraph.archimate3.application;appType=comp;archiType=square and can switch element type through the archiType/appType keys.

tools.name: SysML (sysml) shape library
tools.description: Systems Modeling Language 1.x notation: Model Elements, Blocks, Ports and Flows, Constraint Blocks, Activities, Interactions, State Machines, Use Cases, Allocations, Requirements and Profiles palettes covering block definition, internal block, parametric, requirement, activity and state-machine diagrams. Shapes use prefix mxgraph.sysml and compartments are stack containers.
tools.example: Create a BDD: drag Block (with parts/values/operations compartments) from Blocks and connect blocks with the composite association (endArrow=diamondThin;endFill=1).
tools.notes: For UML-only work prefer uml25; SysML reuses many of its elements with additional stereotypes.

tools.name: Value Stream Mapping (lean_mapping) shape library
tools.description: Lean / value-stream mapping symbols: customer/supplier factory, process box with data box, inventory triangle, supermarket, kanban cards and posts, FIFO lane, push/pull arrows, shipment truck, timeline ladder, kaizen burst, operator and information-flow arrows. Use it for current-state and future-state VSM diagrams.
tools.usage: More Shapes > Business > Value Stream Mapping   |   ?libs=lean_mapping
tools.example: shape=mxgraph.lean_mapping.inventory_box;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;   between two   shape=mxgraph.lean_mapping.manufacturing_process;   boxes; add the timeline with mxgraph.lean_mapping.timeline.
tools.notes: Stencils with prefix mxgraph.lean_mapping; most are recolourable.

tools.name: Cabinets (cabinets) shape library
tools.description: Electrical/control cabinet layout symbols: enclosures, DIN rails, terminal blocks, circuit breakers, contactors, relays, PLC modules, power supplies, cable ducts and panel-mounted controls drawn to scale for panel-layout drawings. Complements the Electrical and PLC ladder palettes.
tools.example: Draw an enclosure, add DIN rails as containers and snap breakers and terminals onto them; set View > Units to mm for real dimensions.
tools.notes: Shapes are stencils with prefix mxgraph.cabinets.

tools.name: Infographic (infographic) shape library
tools.description: Presentation graphics: ribbons, banners, numbered lists, circular and pie segments, arrow steps, timelines, roadmaps, badges, pyramids, funnels, shaded blocks and bar/chart-like shapes with adjustable parameters (dy, dx, arcWidth, ...) exposed in the Property panel. Use it for slides, posters and management summaries rather than technical notation.
tools.example: shape=mxgraph.infographic.ribbonSimple;dy=20;notch=25;fillColor=#10739E;strokeColor=none;html=1;
tools.notes: Many shapes have handles for their parameters; hold Alt while dragging a handle to ignore the grid.

tools.name: Enterprise Integration Patterns (eip) shape library
tools.description: Hohpe/Woolf EIP notation: Message Construction, Message Routing, Message Transformation, Messaging Channels, Messaging Endpoints, Messaging Systems and System Management palettes (message, channel, router, splitter, aggregator, translator, endpoint, dead-letter channel, wire tap, ...). Use it for messaging and integration architecture diagrams (ESB, Kafka, Camel routes).
tools.usage: More Shapes > Other > Enterprise Integration Patterns   |   ?libs=eip
tools.example: shape=mxgraph.eip.content_based_router;html=1;   with   shape=mxgraph.eip.messageChannel;   edges between endpoints.
tools.notes: Stencils with prefix mxgraph.eip.

tools.name: Electrical (electrical) sub-libraries
tools.description: Schematic symbol set with eighteen palettes: LogicGates, Resistors, Capacitors, Inductors, SwitchesRelays, Diodes, Sources (signal sources), Transistors, Misc (miscellaneous), Audio, PlcLadder, Abstract, Optical, VacuumTubes, Waveforms, Instruments, RotMech (rotating/electro-mechanical) and Transmission. Shapes are stencils/JS shapes named mxgraph.electrical.<palette>.<name>; logic gates are one shape (mxgraph.electrical.logic_gates.logic_gate) parameterised by operation=and|or|xor with negation flags.

parameters.name: palettes
parameters.description: logic_gates, resistors, capacitors, inductors, electro_mechanical (switches/relays), diodes, signal_sources, transistors, miscellaneous, audio, plc_ladder, abstract, opto_electronics, vacuum_tubes, waveforms, instruments, rot_mech, transmission (names as used in shape ids).

tools.notes: Components have fixed connection points on their terminals; draw wires with the default connector and endArrow=none. The Fluid Power and Cabinets libraries cover pneumatic/hydraulic and panel layouts.

tools.name: Fluid Power ISO 1219 (fluid_power) shape library
tools.description: Hydraulic and pneumatic circuit symbols according to ISO 1219: pumps, motors, cylinders, directional control valves (with position and actuation elements), pressure/flow control valves, check valves, filters, accumulators, reservoirs, lines and connections. Use it for fluid-power schematics of machines and mobile equipment.
tools.example: Place a 4/3 directional valve, connect P and T to a pump and reservoir and A/B to a double-acting cylinder using straight connectors with endArrow=none.
tools.notes: Valve symbols are composed shapes; use Edit > Edit Style to adjust position count and actuators.

tools.name: Google Material Design (gmdl) shape library
tools.description: Material Design Lite UI components for Android/web mockups: Bottom Navigation, Bottom Sheets, Buttons, Cards, Chips, Dialogs, Dividers, Grid Lists, Icons, Lists, Menus, Misc, Pickers, Progress, Selection Controls, Sliders, Snackbars, Steppers, Tabs, Text Fields, Toolbars and Tooltips palettes. Shapes use prefix mxgraph.gmdl and follow Material metrics.
tools.usage: More Shapes > Other > Google Material Design   |   ?libs=gmdl
tools.example: Build a screen from a Toolbar, a Card list and a floating action Button; set the page to a phone size in File > Page Setup.
tools.notes: For iOS or Bootstrap widgets use the ios, android, bootstrap or mockups libraries.

tools.name: Process Engineering P&ID (pid, pid2) shape libraries
tools.description: Piping and instrumentation diagram symbols. The Process Engineering entry (key pid) offers Agitators, Apparatus Elements, Centrifuges, Compressors, Compressors ISO, Crushers Grinding, Driers, Engines, Feeders, Filters, Fittings, Flow Sensors, Heat Exchangers, Instruments, Misc, Mixers, Piping, Pumps, Pumps DIN, Pumps ISO, Separators, Shaping Machines, Valves and Vessels palettes; the pid2 variant provides the same palettes as parameterised JavaScript shapes (mxgraph.pid2valves.valve, mxgraph.pid2inst.discInst, ...).
tools.usage: More Shapes > Other > Process Engineering   |   ?libs=pid   (parameterised set: pid2)

parameters.name: valveType / actuator / mounting
parameters.description: Keys of the pid2 valve and instrument shapes selecting the symbol variant.

tools.example:
shape=mxgraph.pid2valves.valve;valveType=gate;actuator=man;html=1;
shape=mxgraph.pid2inst.discInst;mounting=field;html=1;
tools.notes: Instrument bubbles take their tag text as the label; piping is drawn with connectors using endArrow=none and strokeWidth=2 for main lines.

tools.name: Threat Modeling (threatModeling) shape library
tools.description: Symbols for STRIDE-style threat models as used by the Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool: external interactor, process, multi-process, data store, data flow, trust boundary (line and box), plus icons for threats and mitigations. Use it with the Data Flow Diagram library to produce threat-model DFDs.
tools.example: Draw processes and data stores, enclose them in a dashed Trust Boundary box (container=1) and label data flows with protocols.
tools.notes: Trust boundaries are dashed containers; set dropTarget=0 if shapes should not become children.

tools.name: Web Icons (webicons) shape library
tools.description: Two palettes of website and brand icons: Web Icons (generic circular icons for RSS, mail, search, chat, share, ...) and Web Logos (logos of common web services and social networks). Use them for sitemaps, integration overviews and marketing diagrams.
tools.example: shape=mxgraph.webicons.github;html=1;   next to   shape=mxgraph.webicons.slack;
tools.notes: Stencils with prefix mxgraph.webicons; logos are trademarks of their owners.

tools.name: Signs (signs) and Clipart (clipart) shape libraries
tools.description: General-purpose pictograms. Signs (stencils, prefix mxgraph.signs.<category>) has Animals, Food, Healthcare, Nature, People, Safety, Science, Sports, Tech, Transportation and Travel palettes of recolourable icons. Clipart (part of the Standard section) provides PNG clip art in computer, finance, clipart, networking, people and telco palettes inserted as shape=image;image=img/clipart/....
tools.usage: More Shapes > Other > Signs   |   ?libs=signs      More Shapes > Standard > Clipart   |   ?libs=clipart
tools.example:
shape=mxgraph.signs.tech.laptop;fillColor=#000000;html=1;
image;aspect=fixed;image=img/clipart/Router_128x128.png;
tools.notes: Clipart images are 128 px PNGs and pixelate when enlarged; prefer Signs or the vector network libraries for scalable output.
